intended_object: The canonical DG functor from the DG category obtained from the A∞ category of a DG category C (with m_n = 0 for n ≥ 3) back to C. It is the identity on objects and sends a degree-n morphism `homLof f` to f, so it is the inverse of the canonical comparison isomorphism (Keller, §3.1). This is inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body uses `EnrichedFunctor.ofDGMap` to build an enriched functor over cochain complexes of R-modules. On objects it is `X ↦ X.as`, the identity on underlying objects. On degree-n morphisms it is the inverse of `aInfinityDGHomEquiv`, the composite of `grHomEquiv` with the inverse of `dgHomEquiv`. That composite sends f to `homLof f`, so its inverse sends `homLof f` to f, as the docstring says.

The proof obligations are:
- compatibility with the differential;
- preservation of identities;
- preservation of composition.

Each is discharged by the corresponding lemma for `aInfinityDGHomEquiv`, so the result really is a DG functor.

The file then proves that this functor and `toAInfinityDGFunctor` compose to the identity in both orders. So it is the stated inverse comparison functor.

The generality is natural: an arbitrary commutative ring R and an arbitrary DG category over R. Mathlib has no A∞ categories, so it has no counterpart.
